content.text: {"primary_meaning":"The presence, glory, and majesty of God—often simultaneously revealing God and concealing the fullness of the divine presence.","primary_basis":["Exodus 13:21–22; 14:19–24 — the pillar of cloud manifests God’s guiding and protecting presence.","Exodus 19:9,16–20; 24:15–18 — the cloud accompanies God’s manifestation at Sinai and covers the mountain with divine glory.","Exodus 40:34–38 — the cloud fills and covers the tabernacle, signifying that God’s glory dwells there.","Leviticus 16:2 — God appears in the cloud above the mercy seat.","1 Kings 8:10–12; 2 Chronicles 5:13–14 — the cloud fills the temple when the glory of the Lord takes possession of it.","Matthew 17:5; Mark 9:7; Luke 9:34–35 — the bright cloud at the Transfiguration signifies God’s presence and communicates the divine voice.","Acts 1:9 — a cloud receives Jesus at the Ascension, commonly interpreted as divine rather than merely meteorological imagery."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"The eschatological coming, heavenly authority, and royal exaltation of the Son of Man or Christ.","basis":["Daniel 7:13–14 — one like a son of man comes with the clouds and receives universal dominion.","Matthew 24:30; 26:64; Mark 13:26; 14:62; Luke 21:27 — Jesus applies cloud-coming imagery to the Son of Man.","Revelation 1:7; 14:14–16 — Christ comes or appears upon the clouds in judgment and kingship."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Divine guidance, protection, and covenant care for God’s people.","basis":["Exodus 13:21–22 — the cloud leads Israel through the wilderness.","Exodus 14:19–20 — the cloud protects Israel by standing between Israel and Egypt.","Numbers 9:15–23; Nehemiah 9:12,19 — the cloud directs Israel’s movements and is remembered as evidence of God’s continuing care.","Psalm 105:39 — God spreads a cloud as a covering."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Judgment, wrath, darkness, or the dread accompanying the day of the Lord.","basis":["Psalm 18:7–12 — dark clouds accompany God’s intervention in judgment.","Isaiah 19:1 — the Lord rides on a swift cloud in judgment upon Egypt.","Ezekiel 30:3,18; 32:7 — clouds and darkness characterize divine judgment.","Joel 2:2; Zephaniah 1:15 — the day of the Lord is described as a day of clouds and thick darkness."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Divine hiddenness, mystery, and the limits of human access to God.","basis":["Exodus 20:21 — Moses approaches the thick darkness where God is.","Deuteronomy 4:11–12 — God speaks from fire, cloud, and thick darkness without a visible form.","Psalm 97:2 — clouds and thick darkness surround God.","1 Timothy 6:16 is often associated conceptually with this theme, although it speaks of unapproachable light rather than a cloud."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Emptiness, unreliability, transience, or promise without fulfillment, especially in the image of clouds that bring no rain.","basis":["Proverbs 25:14 — one who boasts of gifts never given is like clouds without rain.","Hosea 6:4; 13:3 — fleeting faithfulness or life is compared to morning cloud or mist.","2 Peter 2:17 — false teachers are compared to mists driven by a storm.","Jude 12 — false teachers are clouds without rain, swept along by winds."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"The gathered multitude of witnesses surrounding believers.","basis":["Hebrews 12:1 — the 'great cloud of witnesses' is a metaphor for the faithful exemplars named in Hebrews 11."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a broad Christian and scholarly consensus that cloud imagery most characteristically signals divine presence and glory, often combining manifestation with concealment. The symbol is nevertheless context-dependent: clouds can also signify guidance, judgment, eschatological authority, transience, or emptiness. Thus the primary meaning is settled as a general pattern, not as an exclusive meaning in every passage."}
